IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CRIMINAL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CRIMINAL APPEAL NO.              OF 2026
(@ SPECIAL LEAVE PETITION (CRIMINAL) NO. 14330/2026)
DHARMENDER      APPELLANT(S)
VERSUS
STATE OF HARYANA       RESPONDENT(S)
ORDER
1. We have heard  Mr. Narender Hooda,  learned Senior
counsel for the appellant and Mr. Anurag Kulharia, learned
counsel for the respondent-State of Haryana.
2. Leave granted.
3. This  appeal  takes  exception  to  the  order  dated
20.05.2026 passed by the High Court of Punjab and Haryana
(briefly the ‘High Court’ hereinafter), rejecting the
prayer for anticipatory bail of the appellant.
4. Appellant has been arrayed as an accused in FIR
No.263/2025 registered at Police Station- Bawani Khera,
District- Bhiwani, Haryana under Sections 318(4), 338,
336(3), 340(2) and 61(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita,
2023 (for short, ‘BNS’).
5. Appellant  is  a  lawyer  by  profession.  Allegation
against the appellant is that he along with the co-accused
1

--- Page 252 ---
Sansar, had acted in conspiracy to unlawfully transfer the
possession of the land belonging to the complainant to
another person named Meena, who happens to be the wife of
the co-accused.
6. This Court, by order dated 10.08.2026, had issued
notice and granted interim protection to the appellant
subject  to  the  appellant  co-operating  with  the
investigation.
7. Mr. Narender Hooda, learned Senior counsel for the
appellant submits that pursuant to the interim protection
granted by this Court, appellant has appeared before the
Investigating  Officer  and  has  co-operated  with  the
investigation. He further submits that co-accused Sansar
has been granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide the
order dated 24.08.2026. He has also made a statement that
not only has he co-operated with the investigation, he is
willing to hand over his laptop to the investigating
officer, since a grievance has been raised in the counter-
affidavit  of  the  respondent-State  of  Haryana  that
petitioner  had  not  disclosed  the  whereabouts  of  his
laptop.
8. On  the  other  hand,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent-State of Haryana submits that appellant has
misused  his  position  as  a  lawyer  and  had  actively
participated  in  the  fraudulent  activity.  In  such
circumstances, the benefit of pre-arrest bail should not
be granted to the appellant.
2

--- Page 253 ---
9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and on
due consideration, we are of the considered opinion that
the benefit of pre-arrest bail may be extended to the
appellant, subject to the appellant continuing to co-
operate with the investigation and handing over his laptop
to the investigating officer.
10. That being the position, we set aside the impugned
order dated 20.05.2026 passed by the High Court and make
the  order  dated  10.08.2026  absolute.  We  direct  the
appellant to hand over his laptop to the investigating
officer within 07 days from today and also to continue co-
operating with the investigation.
11. Consequently, the Criminal Appeal is allowed.
12. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed
of.

   [UJJAL BHUYAN]
…………………………………………………...J.
     [ATUL S. CHANDURKAR]
NEW DELHI;
06th OCTOBER, 2026.

3. It is the case of the prosecution that on 26.07.2024 at around 11:00 pm,
the appellant, who worked as a private driver at the Block Development
Office, allegedly called the informant’s mother Ruby Devi (who runs a
canteen) at Gwalpada Block Office and fatally strangulated her and
purportedly the home guards on duty, had discovered the said incident. On
completion of the investigation, chargesheet has been filed and trial has
commenced and few of the witnesses have been already examined. The
appellant has been taken into custody on 09.10.2024 and he remains in
custody till date. The defence of the accused is one of total denial and has
been contending that he has been falsely implicated.
1                                                                                     SLP(CRL.) NO.14963 OF 2026

--- Page 260 ---
4. The learned Senior Counsel appearing for the appellant has vehemently
contended that the key prosecution witnesses, namely, the complaint, PW1
and PW3 (Home Guard witnesses) have made contradictory statements and
did not even identify the appellant in the Court during their examination-in-
chief and thereby completely erasing the case of the prosecution. He would
elaborate his submission by contending that complainant himself has
admitted in his cross-examination that he did not draft the written
complaint and it was never read over to him and he had merely affixed the
thumb impression. He would draw the attention of the Court to the
admission of the complainant which is to the effect that he did not
personally witness the incident. Thereby rendering the registration of the
FIR against the appellant, highly suspicious. He would contend that even
the call detail records of the appellant’s mobile, did not reflect any call
having been made on the night of the incident, directly contradicting the
prosecution’s foundation of claim that he had summoned deceased after
calling her to the Block Development Office. Per contra, the learned counsel
appearing for the State would support the impugned order and contend any
scrutiny or examination of the evidence and its evaluation thereof, at this
stage, is likely to prejudice the trial and as such, she would contend that
the testimony of the witnesses taken at its face value, would disentitle the
appellant for grant of bail.
5. Having heard the learned advocates appearing for the parties and
without expressing any opinion on the evidence that has been tendered on
behalf of prosecution witness, we are of the considered view that the
appellant is entitled for being released on bail, since his custody would not
be warranted having regard to the totality of circumstances of the case.
However, we also make it clear that views expressed herein is limited to
grant of bail and it shall in no way prejudice the trial.
2                                                                                     SLP(CRL.) NO.14963 OF 2026

--- Page 261 ---
6. With this observation, we allow the appeal and set aside the impugned
order and direct that a ppellant shall be released on regular bail on such
terms and conditions as the jurisdictional court may deem fit to impose.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

State.
3. The grievance of the petitioner is that by the first
impugned  order  of  28.04.2026  while  suspending  the
sentence of the petitioner, the High Court had imposed
a condition that the fine amount, it has not already
deposited, be deposited. The fine amount in this case
was Rs.87,40,000/-. Thereafter by the second impugned
order of 08.05.2026, on a prayer for keeping the
direction to pay the fine amount in abeyance, the High
Court has modified the earlier order and directed to
deposit of 50% of the fine amount, which is in the tune
of Rs.43,70,000/-.
4. Learned Senior Counsel for the petitioner submits
that  the  condition  is  onerous  and  excessive  and
virtually negates the grant of bail and out of a fixed
sentence  of  10  years,  the  petitioner  has  already
undergone about four years and six months in custody.
5. Learned AAG for the State, however, vehemently
opposes the grant of any relief.
6. Having  considered  the  overall  facts  and
circumstances  of  the  case  and  the  fact  that  the
condition imposed on the petitioner is onerous, we
while maintaining the order of suspension of sentence
and grant of bail, set aside the condition directing

--- Page 284 ---
3
the petitioner to deposit 50% of the fine amount. All
other conditions will remain intact.
7. Accordingly, the sentence of the petitioner shall be
suspended and the petitioner shall be enlarged on bail
subject to the satisfaction of the concerned Trial
Court in connection with the Sessions Trial No.110/2017
for the offences punishable under Sections 409, 467,
471 & 120-B of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section
66 of the Information and Technology Act, 2000.
8. The Special Leave Petitions are disposed of in the
above terms.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the parties on
the prayer for bail.
3. Appellant was convicted by the Trial Court under
Section 302 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for
1

--- Page 307 ---
short, ‘IPC’) and Section 25(1-B)(b) of the Arms
Act, 1959 and sentenced to undergo imprisonment for
life. The conviction and sentence has been affirmed
by the High Court.
4. As per the custody certificate, we find that as
of today, appellant has undergone almost 12 years of
incarceration.
5. Learned counsel for the appellant has drawn the
attention of the Court to the testimony of the
Investigating Officer, i.e. P.W.12, where he stated
that the murder of the deceased at the hands of the
appellant had taken place because of the assault due
to sudden provocation.
6. While learned counsel for the respondent-State of
Madhya Pradesh submits that the theory of sudden
provocation cannot be believed because the appellant
was carrying a knife and in this regard has also
referred to the medical report, we find that both
the  deceased  and  the  appellant  are  not  only
neighbours but also closely related. There was only
a single blow inflicted by the appellant on the
deceased but that was on the neck, which turned out
to be fatal.
7. Having regard to the above and taking an overall
view of the matter, we feel that it would meet the
ends of justice if the appellant is enlarged on
bail, during the pendency of the appeal.
2

--- Page 308 ---
8. Consequently, we direct that the appellant shall
be released on bail on usual terms and conditions.
9. List the appeal for hearing in due course.
10. Liberty granted to the parties to file additional
documents.

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA

VIVEKANANDA REDDY KATAMA               Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
THE REGIONAL PASSPORT OFFICER & ANR.   Respondent(s)
O R D E R
Leave granted.
The appellant, in the instant case, approached
the High Court through a writ petition seeking a
direction for the re-issuance of his passport, on the
premise that mere pendency of criminal cases cannot
be a ground for denial.  The learned Single Judge of
the  High  Court,  vide order  dated  29.04.2024,
dismissed the writ petition, in view of the pending
criminal trial.  The learned Single Judge of the High
Court held that the appellant must first approach the
jurisdictional criminal Court for speedy disposal of
the trial and, thereafter, subject to the final
outcome in the criminal case, he shall approach the
concerned passport authority.  The Division Bench of
the  High  Court,  vide the  impugned  order  dated
06.08.2025, dismissed the writ appeal, reiterating
the holding of the learned Single Judge.

--- Page 313 ---
2
We have heard the learned Counsel appearing for
the appellant and the learned ASG appearing for the
respondent(s).
We hold that the observations made on merits, by
the High Court, shall not stand in the way of the
appellant’s  application  for  No  Objection  in  re-
issuance  of  passport  to  be  filed  before  the
jurisdictional Criminal Court.
The jurisdictional Criminal Court shall decide
the said application, on its own merits, without
being  influenced  by  the  impugned  order  of  the
Division Bench of the High Court dated 06.08.2025 and
the order of the learned Single Judge of the High
Court dated 29.04.2024.  
Accordingly, the appeal stands disposed of, with
the aforesaid directions.
Pending application(s), if any, shall also stand
disposed of.

1

--- Page 334 ---
    
                   
       UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Interim orders passed by the High Court of Allahabad are under
challenge in these special leave petitions. 
2. We have heard Mr. C.S. Vaidyanathan, learned senior counsel
appearing for the State of Uttar Pradesh, Mr. C.A. Sundaram, learned senior
counsel appearing for the U.P. Sugar Mills Association and Mr. Arunabh
Chowdhury, learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner(s) in the
pending Public Interest Litigation before the High Court, at some length.
3. Our attention has been drawn by Mr. Vaidyanathan and Mr.
Sundaram to the order dated 23 rd December, 2021 passed by the Division
Bench of the High Court in an earlier round of litigation which, according to
the High Court, the Cane Commissioner has breached. The relevant part
thereof reads as follows:
“We,  accordingly,  provide  and  direct  that  the
Company/Occupier  should  clear  all  the  dues  of  the
farmers/petitioners herein along with interest @ 15 per cent
per annum on delayed payment, subject to any waiver or
reduction in this regard under Section 17(3) of the Act, 1953 as
discussed, on the principle of ‘first supply, first payment”,
positively,  by  31.03.2022,  failing  which  the  Sugarcane
Commissioner shall proceed to issue recovery certificate to the
Collector for recovery of such dues whereupon the Collectors
shall be under an obligation to recover the said dues by
exercising all means permissible in law including coercive
action against the concerned including the opposite party no.6-
Company and its Directors.”
3. Our attention is also drawn to the order dated 3 rd August, 2026
passed by the Division Bench wherein the assurance of the Cane
Commissioner that the arrears would be recovered with interest @ 15% has
2

--- Page 335 ---
been recorded together with issuance of consequent direction on 30 th July,
2026 for correcting the recovery certificates.
4. Since the judgment dated 23 rd December, 2021 had rightly referred
to Section 17(3) of the U.P. Sugarcane (Regulation of Supply and Purchase)
Act, 1953 permitting waiver or reduction in appropriate cases and,
accordingly, clearance of dues of the farmers was directed to be effected
subject to such waiver/reduction, we grant liberty to the State as well as to
the U.P. Mills Association to remind the High Court of such statutory
mandate together with the observation made in the order dated 23 rd
December, 2021 and dissuade it from insisting on recovery of the dues at a
flat rate of 15% interest. If the State as well as the Association raises such
a plea, we have no doubt that the High Court shall bestow due
consideration to it and pass appropriate orders.
5. With the above observations, the special leave petitions stand
disposed of.
6. All points and contentions on merits are kept open.
7. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
(RAJNI MUKHI)                                   (POOJA KOHLI)

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard learned counsel for the appellant
as well as learned counsel for the respondent-State
of Chhattisgarh.
1

--- Page 361 ---
3. Appellant  was  convicted  by  the  Additional
Sessions Judge, Fast Track Special Court (POCSO Act),
Ambikapur in Special Sessions Case (POCSO) No.12/2018
under Section 376(2)(N) of the Indian Penal Code,
1860 (for short, ‘IPC’) and other sections of the IPC
as  well  as  under  Sections  5(a)(ii)/6  of  the
Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
(for short, ‘POCSO Act’) and sentenced to undergo
Rigorous Imprisonment (for short, ‘R.I.’) for life,
which was explained as imprisonment for the entire
life, till natural death.
4. In appeal, the High Court while affirming the
conviction of the appellant, altered the sentence
awarded under Section 376(2)(N) of the IPC from R.I.
for life till natural death to life imprisonment.
5. This Court, by order dated 03.08.2026, had issued
notice on the Special Leave Petition as well as on
the prayer for bail.
6. In the hearing today, learned counsel for the
appellant  submits  that  appellant  was  arrested
pursuant to his conviction on 14.12.2017 and has
undergone incarceration for almost 09 years as of
now.
7. We find from the materials on record that no DNA
test was carried out to match the DNA profile of the
child with that of the appellant. Paternity test was
also not carried out.
2

--- Page 362 ---
8. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that
the prosecutrix is now residing with the mother of
the appellant.
9. Learned  counsel  for  the  respondent-State  of
Chhattisgarh, on the other hand, fairly submits that
having regard to the facts and circumstances of the
case, the Court may pass appropriate orders.
10. Taking an overall view of the matter, we feel
that it would meet the ends of justice if the
sentence imposed upon the appellant is suspended and
the appellant is enlarged on bail till pendency of
the appeal.
11. Accordingly, we direct that the appellant shall
be enlarged on bail on usual terms and conditions.
12. Appeal be listed for hearing in due course.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Delay condoned.
2. The validity of the ‘Holistic Development of Great Nicobar
Island’ project (GNI Project) is under challenge before the High
Court of Calcutta in a writ petition purportedly filed in public
interest.
3. We have heard learned Attorney General for India, along with
learned  Additional  Solicitor  General  of  India,  and  Dr.  S.
Muralidhar, learned Senior Counsel, who has appeared on caveat, for
the contesting respondents.
4. The High Court order under challenge before us upheld the
maintainability of proceedings challenging GNI Project . Vide  the
impugned order, the High Court has observed that the issue of locus
is flexible in nature and, therefore, the writ petition ought not
to be dismissed at the threshold. We are further informed that
certain other matters raising identical and/or allied issues are
also pending before the High Court. 
5. In such circumstances, learned Attorney General for India,
Additional Solicitor General of India, as well as learned Senior

ITEM NO.29               COURT NO.1               SECTION PIL-W
               S U P R E M E  C O U R T  O F  I N D I A
                       RECORD OF PROCEEDINGS
Writ Petition(s)(Criminal) No(s).386/2026
NALLAPU MANIDEEP                                   Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ANR.                              Respondent(s)
Date : 05-10-2026 This petition was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) : By Courts Motion, AOR
                   
For Respondent(s) : Mr. Sidharth Luthra, Sr. Adv. 
    Mr. Guntur Pramod Kumar, AOR
 Ms. Prerna Singh, Adv.
Mr. Suhail Ahmed, Adv.
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The Petitioner addressed a letter dated 02.09.2026 to one of
us (Surya Kant, CJI.), seeking initiation of suo motu  proceedings
in relation to the unfortunate death of a 7-year-old girl and the
reported  illness  of  several  residents  of  Gollaguppa  Village,
Polavaram District, Andhra Pradesh. It is pointed out, based upon a
news report, that after the anti-malaria tablets (chloroquine) were
administered to the resident of Gollaguppa village, around 52
residents fell ill and were admitted to hospital. It is further
stated that one girl child unfortunately died and 23 other children
were moved to Telangana for medical treatment.
2. Keeping in view the seriousness of the issue and the averments
to the effect that administration of chloroquine tablets during an
1

--- Page 740 ---
anti-malaria drive may have allegedly led to the unfortunate death
of the girl child and hospitalisation of several others, we have
taken suo motu notice of the concerns raised in the letter.
3. Mr. Sidharth Luthra, learned Senior Counsel for the State of
Andhra Pradesh, at the outset, has informed that the authorities
have already taken cognizance of the incident and a criminal case
has been registered. He has further informed that the viscera
report is still awaited.
4. It seems to us that the matter warrants judicial oversight
until the ongoing investigation is taken to its logical conclusion.
We are, however, of the view that High Court of Andhra Pradesh
would be the appropriate forum to monitor the investigation and any
consequential proceedings.
5. Consequently, we transfer these proceedings to the High Court
of Andhra Pradesh, with a request to the Hon'ble Chief Justice of
the High Court to take up the matter on a priority basis.
6. The Writ Petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
7. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
(ARJUN BISHT)                              (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
ASTT. REGISTRAR-cum-PS                        DY. REGISTRAR

Writ Petition(s)(Civil) No(s).1114/2026
UJJAWAL GAUR                                       Petitioner(s)
                                VERSUS
UNION OF INDIA & ORS.                              Respondent(s)
IA No. 265715/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 05-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :  Petitioner-in-person
                    
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner is a practicing advocate. He has filed this
petition, purportedly in public interest, seeking directions for
effective  flood  management  in  Assam  and  to  take  immediate
preventive  measures  to  ensure  compliance  with  the  existing
statutory obligations. The petitioner has adverted to the statutory
framework dealing with the issue, but is aggrieved by the fact
that, despite the Brahmaputra Board Act, 1980, being in force the
mandate contemplated under Sections 12 and 13 thereof, including
the conduct of scientific surveys and investigations and the
preparation and revision of Master Plans, has not been duly
implemented. He has also highlighted the River Boards Act, 1956,
and  the  Assam  Embankment  and  Drainage  Act,  1953,  whereunder
mechanisms for coordinated river management and the construction,
1

--- Page 744 ---
maintenance and protection of flood control infrastructure has been
laid down.
2. We have heard the petitioner-in-person. 
3. It seems to us that various suggestions made and deficiencies
pointed out by the petitioner ought, in the first instance, to be
placed before the competent authorities. We are of the view that
the issue is not essentially legal in nature; rather, they call for
coordinated consideration and action by the concerned authorities
to ensure that adequate measures are taken to prevent recurring
floods, riverbank erosion or drainage congestion in Assam.
4. We, consequently, without expressing any opinion on merits,
dispose of this writ petition with a direction to the Registry of
this Court to forward copies of this writ petition to all the
respondents,  who  shall  look  into  the  suggestions/grievances
expressed by the petitioner and may take appropriate remedial
measures. The petitioner shall deposit requisite copies of the
paper book with the Registry of this Court to comply with this
order. 
5. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

SANTOSH & ORS.                                     Petitioner(s)

STATE OF RAJASTHAN & ORS.                          Respondent(s)
IA No. 289458/2026 - EXEMPTION FROM FILING O.T.
 
Date : 05-10-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :Mr. H. D. Thanvi, Adv.
                   Mr. Nikhil Kumar Singh, Adv.
                   Mr. Kshitish Bikarmia, Adv.
                   Mr. Rishi Matoliya- 2217, AOR
                                      
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. We  have  heard  learned  counsel  for  the  petitioners  at
considerable length and have also perused the material on record. 
2. The issue pertains to earmarking of 10 hectares of land
forming part of Khasra No. 391 (subject land) for the purpose of
construction of Deedwana-Kuchaman District Jail. It emerges from
the record that, initially, 6 hectares of land situated at Village
Aajwa was identified by the District Collector for the said
purpose, but the proposal could not be approved as the land fell
within a catchment area. Thereafter, the subject land was earmarked
1

--- Page 746 ---
and approved for the construction of the District Jail. In the
impugned order High Court has noted that out of approximately 29
hectares of land recorded as pasture land, only 10 hectares have
been earmarked for the construction of the District Jail. Further,
in lieu thereof, alternative pasture land has been earmarked for
compensatory purposes. 
3. In such circumstances, we find that the construction of a
District Jail is essentially in larger public interest, therefore,
the view taken by the High Court does not warrant any interference.
4. At the same time, we grant liberty to the petitioners to
pursue their cause for allotment of compensatory pasture land in
closer proximity to their village. Any such representation/claim in
this  regard,  pending  before  the  authority,  be  considered
expeditiously and sympathetically.
5. The Special Leave Petition is, accordingly, disposed of.
6. Pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
(ARJUN BISHT)                             (PREETHI DILEEP KUMAR)
